subject: direct and indirect effects for SEM

messages.author: 4472c95c744fee6b
messages.subject: direct and indirect effects for SEM
parts:
Hi there,

I have two questions about indirect and direct effects in a SEM. It is more about Mplus, but my question derives from a ppt that I found that was presented by Yves Rosseel, so I thought it would be ok to post it here.

1- Suppose that I have an exogenous dummy variable with four categories (x0 as a reference group), a mediator latent variable (z) and an outcome latent variable (y), could I simply obtain indirect and direct effects by using the IND command of Mplus:

Y IND X1;

Y IND X2;

Y IND X3;

 

2- Similarly, if I have an exogenous dummy variable with four categories (x0 as a reference group), a mediator latent variable (z1) that lead to another mediator latent variable (z2) and an outcome latent variable (y) (so the model will look like X –> Z1 -> Z2 -> Y), could I still simply obtain indirect and direct effects by using the IND command of Mplus:

Y IND X1;

Y IND X2;

Y IND X3;


The reason I ask, is that I found a ppt of Yves Rosseel saying “Imai et al. (2010) showed in a simulation study that the naive approach (taking the product of coefﬁcients) results in biased estimates of the direct and indirect effects” (ppt 24/32). However, this information was placed after a section called “Mediation with an ordinal mediation, and a binary outcome”. Thus, I’m not sure if this “critic” applies to my project ...

Link for the ppt :http://www.da.ugent.be/cvs/pages/en/Presentations/Presentation%20Yves%20Rosseel.pdf

Thank you!
